title: Medicine levels in blood (valproate, lithium, digoxin)
what: This blood test shows how much of a medicine is in your blood right now. It tells your doctor if the dose is enough and not too high.
why: For medicines with a narrow safe range, after a dose change, with side effects, or if a medicine is not helping.
duration: the blood draw usually takes 5 minutes; results usually come in 1 to 2 days
tell_doctor: The exact time of your last dose
If you missed any doses in the last few days
If you had vomiting, diarrhea, dehydration, or fever

prepare.title: Timing
prepare.text: The time of the draw matters most. Blood is usually taken just before your next dose. Your doctor will tell you the exact time.

prepare.title: Morning dose
prepare.text: Ask your doctor whether to take your morning dose before or after the test. Do not skip or change a dose on your own.

prepare.title: Regularity
prepare.text: For several days before the test, take your medicine exactly on schedule.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: You usually do not need to fast. Check with the lab.

bring: The time of your last dose, written down
Your medicine, if the doctor said to take it after the test
steps: Tell the nurse when you last took the medicine
A band is tied above your elbow
The skin is wiped with antiseptic
Blood is taken from a vein into a tube
The draw time is written on the referral
feel: A quick prick, like a pinch
Sometimes slight dizziness. Tell the nurse, and they will help you lie down
after: Press the cotton pad for 3 to 5 minutes
Take your medicine, if your doctor said so
Results usually come in 1 to 2 days
Only your doctor changes the dose based on the result
red_flags: Severe shaking, vomiting, diarrhea, unsteadiness, or confusion: see a doctor right away
Fainting, seizures, or a very irregular heartbeat: call emergency services

faq.q: Why does the test time matter?
faq.a: Right after a dose, there is a lot of medicine in your blood, and then it drops. Without the exact time, the result is easy to misread.

faq.q: How often is this test done?
faq.a: More often at the start of treatment and after a dose change, then less often. Your doctor will give you a schedule.

reminders.text: Medicine level test tomorrow. Write down the time of your last dose. Take your morning dose as your doctor said.
